Ransomware Attack Disrupts Icelandic Transportation & Logistics Sector

A large-scale ransomware attack has severely disrupted operations across Iceland’s transportation and logistics sector, with leading firms reporting halted shipments and widespread IT outages as of Thursday morning.

The attack, first detected late Wednesday, has affected several major logistics providers, including Norðurljós Freight and Arctic Haulage, according to the Icelandic Association of Transport Companies. “Our members are facing significant operational challenges,” said association spokesperson Björn Kristjánsson. “Several firms are unable to process shipments or access key customer records. The situation is evolving rapidly.”

While the full extent of the breach remains unclear, sources familiar with the incident say attackers encrypted vast portions of companies’ IT systems, demanding payment in cryptocurrency to restore access. “We are working around the clock with cybersecurity experts and authorities,” said Helga Eiríksdóttir, CEO of Norðurljós Freight, in a statement. “At present, we cannot estimate when normal operations will resume.”

The disruption has delayed road and sea cargo shipments across the country, with Reykjavík’s main logistics terminals reporting significant backlogs. “Some clients awaiting critical parts and supplies have already experienced 24-hour delays,” said Sigurður Hjartarson, a union representative for logistics workers. “The impact is being felt in both urban and remote areas.”

The National Police Commissioner confirmed an ongoing investigation. “This is a serious incident with implications for Iceland’s supply chains,” said a police spokesperson.

Analysts warn that continued disruption could lead to shortages and higher costs if not resolved swiftly. “This attack underscores the vulnerability of the sector’s digital infrastructure,” said transportation analyst Guðrún Ólafsdóttir. “Resilience planning will be crucial going forward.”
